JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 18.11.2020.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 18.11.2020 at about 6.30 a.m., the petitioner was going towards his shop at Karanjikatte from APMC market, Kolar by riding TVS XL moped bearing No. KA- 07-R-3573 on Malur-Kolar road, in front of APMC market, at that time the driver of Ashok Leyland light goods vehicle bearing No.KA-07-B-1329 came from opposite direction from Kolar town in a wrong side of one way road in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle went to its wrong side and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to SNR Hospital, Kolar wherein he was admitted as inpatient and spent huge amount towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as shopkeeper and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner suffering from permanent disability and he is unable to lead the normal life.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle
are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondent No.1 remained absent hence, placed exparte.

Respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-07-B-1329 and the liability of this respondent, if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
The accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of petitioner himself.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the claim petition against them.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 18.11.2020 at 6.30 a.m. due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Ashok Leyland light goods vehicle bearing No. KA-07-B- Erappa vs Ranjith R on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24917929/
and in the said accident peti- tioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner is examined as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 7.
In spite of sufficient opportunities, the respondents have not lead any evidence.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 :

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 :

As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
8. ISSUE NO.1 : That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed affidavit in lieu of-examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, PW.1 produced true copies of FIR with complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet, all these documents are marked under Ex.P.1 to P.5.
9.
As per the documents, the contents of Ex.P.1- FIR with complaint supports the claim of the petitioner in respect of occurrence of the accident.
The first information is given by the petitioner himself while taking treatment in the hospital.
The FIR was registered on the same day of alleged accident.

As per Ex.P.1 it is alleged that the Ashok leyland light goods vehicle bearing No.
KA-07-B-1329 came to the wrong side of the road and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
As per the contents of Ex.P.2 mahazar, the accident was caused towards Malur-Kolar one sided road.

This shows that the driver of Ashok leyland light goods vehicle bearing No.
KA-07-B-1329 came to its wrong side and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
As per Ex.P.3 IMV report, no visible damages were found on Ashok leyland light goods vehicle bearing No.KA-07-B-1329 but, the motorcycle of the petitioner got damages in its front side.

This once again helped the petitioner to show that the driver of Ashok leyland light goods vehicle bearing No.
KA-07-B-1329 came to his wrong side and dashed against the motorcycle.
The contents of Ex.P.2 mahazar and Ex.P.3 IMV report helped the petitioner to prove the alleged negligence of driver of Ashok layland light goods vehicle bearing No. KA-07-B-1329.
The respondent no.1 being the owner of the said Ashok leyland light goods vehicle bearing No. KA-07-B-1329 remained absent.

Even though the Pw.1 is cross-examined by the respondent No.2, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW.1 to hold that there was no negligence or rash driving by the driver of the insured Ashok layland light goods vehicle bearing No.KA-07-B-1329.

No rebuttal evidence is placed by the Erappa vs Ranjith R on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24917929/
3 respondents.
10.
As per the averments of the petition the accident was occurred on 18.11.2020 at about 6.30 p.m and immediately the petitioner was shifted to SNR Hospital, Kolar.
The FIR was also came to be registered on the date of alleged accident itself.
11. No evidence is made available by the respondents to disbelieve the contents of Ex.P4 wound certificate and Ex.P6 Discharge summary.

12. Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-5 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Ashok leyland light goods vehicle bearing No. KA-07-B-1329.

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima- facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW-1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW-1 and AW-2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.

The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.

The registration of FIR and filing of the charge-sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.
(Emphasis supplied by me)

13. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a Erappa vs Ranjith R on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24917929/
4 particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even here in this case the driver of the offending vehicle is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the offending vehicle and he was charge sheeted.

14. By the above said reasons it can be held that there is a negligence on the part of the driver of the Ashok leyland light goods vehicle bearing No. KA-07-B- 1329 and his negligence is the sole reason for the said accident.
15.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 18.11.2020 which is caused by the driver of Ashok leyland light goods vehicle bearing No. KA-07-B-1329 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
16.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.

17. The petitioner has produced wound certificate summary as per Ex.P4 which shows that the petitioner sustained four simple injuries and one grievous injury Further the petitioner has also produced discharge summary as per Ex.P6 which shows that the petitioner admitted to the S.N.R.
District Hospital, Kolar on 18.11.2020 and discharged on 25.11.2020.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him at the time of accident.
Without the evidence of doctor, it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained disability due to grievous injuries.
18. According to the petitioner he was working as shopkeeper and was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
To prove his avocation and income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.

19. While determining the compensation this court has to look into the pain and sufferings, medical expenses, diet, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges and loss of amenities and enjoyment of life that the PW-1 has suffered, which are discussed herein below:
Erappa vs Ranjith R on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24917929/
5 (A) TOWARDS PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The petitioner has relied upon Ex.P.4-wound certificate and Ex.P6- discharge summary, which make it crystal clear that PW-1 has sustained injuries in the accident.

entities.text: Erappa vs Ranjith R on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence keeping in mind the injury mentioned in wound certificate, it can be said that the petitioner must have undergone some amount of physical pain and sufferings, for which, an amount of Rs.50,000/- can be held to be just and proper compensation under this head.

(B) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has not produced medical bills hence, he is not entitled for compensation under this head.

(C) TOWARDS DIET, FOOD, NOURISHMENT,
ATTENDANT AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
As already observed the Ex.P-1, makes it amply clear that the petitioner underwent treatment for the injuries sustained by her.
During the said period the petitioner might have taken assistance from others and taken diet food.
On consideration of the injuries sustained by the petitioner this Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award an amount of Rs.25,000/- under this head.
(D) TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING CAPACITY ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
It is necessary to note that the loss of future earning capacity cannot be presumed and has to be proved with cogent evidence.

But interestingly the petitioner though claims that she is unable to do any work and has become permanently disabled she has not put in any efforts to prove the disability by examining the doctor, who treated her.
In fact she has not even produced the disability certificate issued by competent authority.
In the absence of any such material piece of evidence, it is very difficult for this Court to assess the disability and thereby assess the loss of earning capacity due to disability.
This makes it clear that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability.

Hence, this court has no option but to hold that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability which has resulted in reduction of his salary and hence she is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
(E) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as shop keeper and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
But no evidence is placed in this regard.

Such being the case, it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.14,500/-
p.m. as the accident is of the year 2020.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.6 the petitioner was admitted to S.N.R. hospital, Kolar from 18.11.2020 to 25.11.2020 for a period of 7 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be Erappa vs Ranjith R on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24917929/
6 considered.
As such in the absence of evidence in this regard , this court is of the opinion that in total 3 months period including 5 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,500/- X 3 months = Rs.43,500/- during the laid up period.
(F) TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES AND ENJOYMENT OF LIFE:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by her, which might certainly have deprived her of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award him a reasonable sum of Rs.25,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 50,000/-
b. Towards medical expenses NIL c.

Towards Diet, Food, Nourishment Rs. 25,000/-
 and conveyance charges d. Towards loss of future earning NIL  capacity on account of permanent  disability e. Towards loss of income during Rs. 43,500/-
 laid up period f.

Towards loss of amenities and Rs. 25,000/-
 enjoyment of life
Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 and 2 are the Owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Ashok Leyland light goods vehicle bearing No. KA-07- B-1329.
No other grounds are made out by showing the violation of policy conditions by respondent No.1 owner.
The petitioner has not produced his driving license.
The accident was caused by the driver of Ashok Leyland light goods vehicle bearing No. KA-07-B-1329 by coming in the wrong side.
Hence, merely because the petitioner does not produced driving license, the contributory negligence cannot be considered.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs. 1,43,500/- (Rupees One lakh Forty Three Thousand and Five hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
